title: Dissipative Time Crystals as Passively Protected Oscillating Qubits
summary: Passive error correction schemes have so far been limited to static memories rather than dynamical qubits. We demonstrate that a driven-dissipative bosonic system, the Bose-Hubbard dimer (BHD), can encode a persistently oscillating qubit within a dynamical noiseless subsystem (DNS). The strong parity symmetry of the system leads to degenerate stationary states, whose mutual coherence breaks the time translation symmetry, giving rise to a time crystal in the thermodynamic limit.
